tcs.test_item:
Before initiating an audio source transition, the Audio Management software shall terminate all active media operations, including mute, seek, fast-forward, rewind, scan, tuning, PTY operations, disc operations, and audio setup activities

(Confirm every active media function is cancelled before the source transition starts)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an FM station and start a "SEEK" operation
2. Select a different audio source while the seek is still running
3. Read the state of the seek operation and record it
4. Record the order of the seek operation end and the source transition start
tcs.expected_result:
1. FM audio plays and the seek operation runs
2. The source selection is accepted
3. The seek operation is cancelled
4. The source transition starts with no media function still active
tcs.design_method: 情境 / 用例 (Scenario / Use Case Testing)
tcs.reasoning: 4866468 lists the media functions to interrupt; SEEK is chosen as the representative because the SWE.1 Verification Method names seek and scan.

tcs.test_item:
Before initiating an audio source transition, the Audio Management software shall terminate all active media operations, including mute, seek, fast-forward, rewind, scan, tuning, PTY operations, disc operations, and audio setup activities

(Confirm a running scan is cancelled by the same transition path as a seek)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an FM station and start a "SCAN" operation
2. Select a different audio source while the scan is still running
3. Record the order of the scan cancellation and the source transition
tcs.expected_result:
1. FM audio plays and the scan operation runs
2. The source selection is accepted
3. The scan operation is cancelled and no media function remains active
tcs.design_method: 情境 / 用例 (Scenario / Use Case Testing)
tcs.reasoning: Second function from the 4866468 list, kept separate so a pass on seek cannot mask a failure on scan.

tcs.test_item:
Before initiating an audio source transition, the Audio Management software shall terminate all active media operations, including mute, seek, fast-forward, rewind, scan, tuning, PTY operations, disc operations, and audio setup activities

(Confirm a disc operation is cancelled by the same pre-transition sweep)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play a disc and start a disc up operation
2. Select a different audio source while the disc operation is running
3. Record the state of the disc operation
tcs.expected_result:
1. The disc plays and the disc up operation runs
2. The source selection is accepted
3. The disc operation is cancelled
tcs.design_method: 情境 / 用例 (Scenario / Use Case Testing)
tcs.reasoning: Third member of the 4866468 function list, after seek and scan. Disc operations run on a different subsystem from tuner operations, so they can survive a sweep that clears the others.

tcs.test_item:
When the Entertainment audio source is deactivated, the Audio Management software shall apply a gradual volume ramp-down to mute using the configured ramp-down timing parameters

(Confirm Entertainment audio is ramped down to mute over the specified ramp duration)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play an Entertainment source at a fixed volume
2. Select another Entertainment source
3. Measure the time between the start of the level decrease and silence
4. Compare the measured ramp-down time against the specification and record the outcome
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays at the set volume
2. The new source selection is accepted
3. The Entertainment level decreases gradually to mute within 25 ms to 50 ms
4. The measured ramp-down time is within 25 ms to 50 ms
tcs.reasoning: 4866469 states the ramp-down uses <Tent Ramp Down>; the value is taken from CFTS019-4867767, so the step carries a real bound and not a placeholder.

tcs.test_item:
After completion of the source transition sequence, the Audio Management software shall activate the newly selected Entertainment audio source

(Confirm the newly selected Entertainment source becomes active once the transition completes)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play Entertainment source A
2. Select Entertainment source B
3. Wait until the ramp-down of source A has completed
4. Record which Entertainment source is active
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment source A plays
2. The selection of source B is accepted
3. Source A is muted
4. Source B is the active Entertainment source
tcs.reasoning: 4866470 is the activation step of the sequence; the check is placed after ramp-down completion because that is the ordering the clause states.

tcs.test_item:
After completing the Entertainment audio ramp-down, the Audio Management software shall maintain the audio output in the muted state for the configured mute hold duration before initiating the ramp-up sequence

(Confirm the mute is held for ramp-down plus amplifier mute plus ramp-up before audio returns)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play Entertainment source A
2. Select Entertainment source B
3. Measure the interval during which the output stays muted
4. Compare the measured mute interval against the sum of the three specified intervals and record the outcome
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment source A plays
2. The selection of source B is accepted
3. The output stays muted for the ramp-down (25 ms to 50 ms), the amplifier mute (at most 100 ms) and the ramp-up (25 ms to 50 ms)
4. The measured mute interval matches the sum of the three specified intervals
tcs.reasoning: 4866471 composes the hold from <Tent Ramp Down> + <Tmute amp> + <Tent Ramp Up>; all three have spec values (4867767, 4867773, 4867766), so the whole sum is spec-sourced.

tcs.test_item:
Upon activation of a new Entertainment source, the Audio Management software shall update the $HUModeStatus$ signal to reflect the current active Entertainment source

(Confirm the mode status signal reports the new Entertainment source once ramp-down completes)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play Entertainment source A
2. Select Entertainment source B
3. Record $HUModeStatus$ from the vehicle bus
4. Read $HUModeStatus$ at the moment the ramp-down completes and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment source A plays
2. The selection of source B is accepted
3. $HUModeStatus$ is transmitted
4. $HUModeStatus$ reports source B immediately after the ramp-down completes
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 $HUModeStatus$ not found in the supplied DBC; signal name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4866472 names $HUModeStatus$ but the supplied DBC carries no such signal and no variant of it, so the name is kept verbatim per R-13 (g) and the gap is raised as DR-AM4 rather than resolved by substituting a lookalike.

tcs.test_item:
Following completion of the mute hold period, the Audio Management software shall restore the recalled Entertainment volume by applying a controlled volume ramp-up using the configured ramp-up timing parameters

(Confirm Entertainment audio ramps back up to the recalled volume within the specified time)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play Entertainment source A at volume level 20
2. Select Entertainment source B
3. Wait until the mute hold has completed
4. Measure the ramp-up time and the final volume
5. Compare the measured ramp-up time against the specification and read the restored volume level
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment source A plays at volume level 20
2. The selection of source B is accepted
3. The output is muted for the hold interval
4. The Entertainment level increases to volume level 20 within 25 ms to 50 ms
5. The measured ramp-up time is within 25 ms to 50 ms and the volume is level 20
tcs.reasoning: 4866477 ties the ramp-up to <Tent Ramp Up> and to the recalled volume; volume level 20 is an arbitrary but fixed level so the recall is observable.

tcs.test_item:
Before deactivating the current Entertainment source, the Audio Management software shall issue a Pause request to the active media source when the source supports pause functionality

tcs.reasoning: 4866492 qualifies the pause with "if possible", so a pause-capable source (USB media) is used to make the positive case observable.

Prior to Entertainment source deactivation, the Audio Management software shall terminate all active media control operations, including seek, scan, fast-forward, rewind, tuning, PTY operations, disc operations, and audio setup activities

tcs.test_item:

tcs.test_item:

tcs.test_item:
When a signal source becomes active, the Audio Management software shall ramp up the signal audio on the configured output channels using the configured Ramp-Up parameters

tcs.test_item:
When no source is active and a new Entertainment or Information source becomes active, the Audio Management software shall ramp the new source from mute to the configured playback level using the configured Ramp-Up duration

tcs.test_item:

tcs.test_item:
When an Entertainment or Information audio source becomes inactive, the Audio Management software shall ramp down the corresponding audio output using the configured Entertainment Ramp Down or Information Ramp Down duration through the VolumeShaper API

(Confirm a deactivating source is ramped down over the duration its own type specifies)
tcs.test_procedure:

2. Deactivate the Entertainment source
3. Measure the ramp-down time
4. Measure the ramp-down time and record it
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment audio plays
2. The deactivation is accepted
3. The Entertainment level decreases gradually
4. The measured ramp-down time is within the value the specification defines for this source type

tcs.reasoning: 4866844 writes <Temt Ramp Down>, which the specification never defines; the only defined entertainment ramp-down is <Tent Ramp Down> at 4867767. The execution layer does not infer, so the bound is left to the PENDING and the reading is proposed as A-AM04.

tcs.test_item:
When an Entertainment or Information audio source becomes inactive, the Audio Management software shall ramp down the corresponding audio output using the configured Entertainment Ramp Down or Information Ramp Down duration through the VolumeShaper API

tcs.test_item:
When switching from one Entertainment source to another, the Audio Management software shall ramp down the currently active Entertainment source using the configured Entertainment Ramp Down duration before activating the new Entertainment source

tcs.test_item:
During an Entertainment source transition, the Audio Management software shall wait for a duration equal to Entertainment Ramp Down + Amplifier Mute Time + Entertainment Ramp Up before enabling playback of the new Entertainment source. During this period, the Entertainment output channel shall remain muted

(Confirm the output stays muted for the whole transition delay and the new source waits for it)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play Entertainment source A
2. Select Entertainment source B
3. Record the state of the output channel for the Entertainment source
4. Measure the interval between the end of source A and the first audio of source B
5. Record the output state throughout the delay and the moment source B first produces audio
tcs.expected_result:
1. Entertainment source A plays
2. The selection of source B is accepted
3. The output channel for the Entertainment source is muted
4. The interval covers the entertainment ramp-down, the amplifier mute (at most 100 ms) and the entertainment ramp-up (25 ms to 50 ms)
5. Source B produces no audio before the delay expires
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM5 <Temp Ramp Down> value not defined in available sources
tcs.reasoning: 4866855 sums <Temp Ramp Down> + <Tmute AMP> + <Tent Ramp Up>. Two of the three resolve (4867773, 4867766); the first does not, so the sum carries the PENDING while the mute-throughout behaviour is still checked.

tcs.test_item:

tcs.expected_result:

tcs.reasoning: 4866856 is the ramp-up half of the Ent to Ent axis and binds to <Tent Ramp Up>, which resolves at 4867766, so this case needs no PENDING.

tcs.test_item:
When an Entertainment source becomes active, the Audio Management software shall update the current Entertainment source status, transmit the current Entertainment volume, and route the Entertainment audio stream to the amplifier

(Confirm activation updates the mode status, sends the volume and routes audio to the amplifier)
tcs.test_procedure:
1. Play no audio source
2. Activate an Entertainment source
3. Record $HUModeStatus$ and $VolumeENT$ from the vehicle bus
4. Read $HUModeStatus$ and record it
5. Read $VolumeENT$ and record it
6. Record the audio stream present at the amplifier input
tcs.expected_result:
1. No audio source is active
2. The Entertainment source starts
3. $HUModeStatus$ and $VolumeENT$ are transmitted
4. $HUModeStatus$ reports the active Entertainment source
5. $VolumeENT$ carries the current Entertainment volume
6. The amplifier receives the Entertainment audio stream
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 $HUModeStatus$ not found in the supplied DBC; signal name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g); PENDING: DR-AM4 $VolumeENT$ not found in the supplied DBC; signal name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4866874 requires three outcomes at once, so they are checked in one case rather than split. Neither $HUModeStatus$ nor $VolumeENT$ is in the supplied DBC, and the DBC carries no volume signal at all, so both names stay verbatim per R-13 (g) under DR-AM4.

tcs.test_item:
When a TA/PTY31 Entertainment source becomes active, the Audio Management software shall update HUModeStatus according to the active radio source (DAB, SDAR, or FM), transmit the current TA/PTY31 volume, and route the audio stream to the amplifier

3. Record $HUModeStatus$ from the vehicle bus

2. The traffic announcement starts
3. $HUModeStatus$ is transmitted
4. $HUModeStatus$ reports "DAB_Selected"
5. The amplifier receives the announcement audio
tcs.remarks: PENDING: DR-AM4 $HUModeStatus$ not found in the supplied DBC; signal name kept as written in CFTS019 per R-13 (g)
tcs.reasoning: 4866875 maps the TA source onto three status values; the DAB row is taken here and the FM row in the second case, so each mapping is exercised without one masking the other. The label is quoted verbatim from the clause because the DBC has no entry to check it against.

tcs.test_item:
The Audio Management software shall ramp up Entertainment audio using VolumeShaper within 25 ms to 50 ms

(Confirm the entertainment ramp-up does not complete before the lower bound)

tcs.expected_result:
